findings.evidence: <input id="acctnum-input" name="account_number" type="text" required="">, in a form headed Set up your account with submit label Create account
findings.fix: Remove the Account number field from account creation, or explain that it links an existing account and make it optional.
findings.violation: A required Account number field asks a person creating a brand new account for a number that an account not yet created cannot have, and the form states no reason the account-creation task needs it.

findings.evidence: <input id="org-input" name="organization" type="text" style="font-size:16px" required="">, in a form otherwise collecting a personal name, email, password and home address
findings.fix: Make the Organization name field optional, or remove it if the account task does not need business details.
findings.violation: Organization name is required though the rest of the form collects an individual's personal details, so a person signing up without a business has no truthful value to enter.

findings.evidence: <select id="shipspeed-select" required=""><option>Standard</option><option>Express</option><option>Overnight</option></select>, inside a form headed Set up your account with no order or cart in progress
findings.fix: Remove the shipping-speed choice from account creation and ask it during checkout instead.
findings.violation: A required Preferred shipping speed choice is forced during account creation, though shipping speed is a decision an order needs, not an account, and it could be asked when the person actually places one.

findings.evidence: <input id="website-input" name="website" type="url" required="">, in a form otherwise collecting a personal name, email, password and home address
findings.fix: Make the Company website field optional, or remove it if the account task does not need business details.
findings.violation: Company website is required though the rest of the form collects an individual's personal details, so a person signing up without a business has no truthful value to enter.

findings.fix: Say beside the field what the number is used for, or make it optional.
findings.violation: A phone number is required with no word beside the field on why it is needed, though the form already asks for an email address.

findings.fix: Move the rule into hint text beside the field, linked with aria-describedby.
findings.violation: A format rule appears only in the placeholder, which disappears as soon as typing starts.

findings.fix: Mark the optional fields with the word optional in their labels, or mark the required ones and explain the mark.

instances.evidence: <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="password-input" name="password" type="password" autocomplete="new-password" required="" minlength="6">
<input id="street-input" name="street_address" type="text" autocomplete="address-line1" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">
<input id="given-input" name="given_name" type="text" autocomplete="given-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">
<input id="family-input" name="family_name" type="text" autocomplete="family-name" autocorrect="off" spellcheck="false" required="">

findings.violation: The form mixes 14 required and 1 optional fields and marks none of them, so the person cannot tell which may be left empty.
A control that clears everything entered sits directly beside the submit button.

findings.fix: Raise the button's padding and font size so its rendered box is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels.
findings.violation: The View details button's declared padding of 1px by 2px and font size of 11px render a tap target of roughly 15 CSS pixels tall, far below the roughly 44 pixel size a fingertip needs, so a tap aimed at it easily misses.

findings.evidence: <button id="reset-btn" type="reset">Clear form</button> beside <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">Create account</button>, neither carrying a style or class attribute
findings.fix: Style the reset button as visibly lesser than the submit button, for example as a plain text link or outlined button, so the primary action is the obvious one to press.
findings.violation: The secondary action Clear form carries no style distinguishing it from the primary action Create account, so both render as identical default buttons and a person must read each label to find the one that saves their entry.

findings.fix: Remove the field from account creation and ask for a preferred contact time only when a contact is actually being scheduled.
findings.violation: A required Preferred contact time is collected at account creation, though this answer is only useful at the point the business actually needs to call the person, which could be asked then instead.

findings.evidence: <input id="family-input" name="family_name" type="text" autocomplete="family-name" required="">, after the form already collected <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required="">
findings.fix: Keep only one name request, either the single Full name field or the split given and family name fields, and remove the other.
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name twice: once as Full name near the top, then again as a separate required Last name field further down, so the person retypes identity data the form already has.

findings.evidence: <input id="given-input" name="given_name" type="text" autocomplete="given-name" required="">, after the form already collected <input id="name-input" name="full_name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required="">
findings.fix: Keep only one name request, either the single Full name field or the split given and family name fields, and remove the other.
findings.violation: The form asks for the person's name twice: once as Full name near the top, then again as a separate required First name field further down, so the person retypes identity data the form already has.

findings.evidence: <input id="member-input" name="membership_number" type="text" inputmode="numeric" placeholder="Must be 8 digits" required="">
findings.fix: Make the field optional for people joining without a prior membership, or state in hint text where to find the number and why account creation needs it.
findings.violation: A required Membership number field asks every new signee for a pre-existing number with no explanation of what it is or what a signee without one should do, though the task at hand is creating the account itself.
